title: Leviticus 22: The Holy Things and Offerings Without Blemish
body:
Read the chapter → [Leviticus 22](/bible/leviticus/22)

## Introduction

This reading covers [Leviticus 22](/bible/leviticus/22) through 25: the holy things of the priests and the law of offerings without blemish, the feasts of the Lord, the pure oil and the shewbread and the judgment of the blasphemer, and the sabbath of the land with the year of jubile. All four chapters were read, with precepts brought in along the way and questions answered after the reading.

**[Leviticus 22:1-3](/bible/leviticus/22#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/leviticus/22#v1)</sup> And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/leviticus/22#v2)</sup> Speak unto Aaron and to his sons, that they separate themselves from the holy things of the children of Israel, and that they profane not my holy name in those things which they hallow unto me: I am the Lord.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/leviticus/22#v3)</sup> Say unto them, Whosoever he be of all your seed among your generations, that goeth unto the holy things, which the children of Israel hallow unto the Lord, having his uncleanness upon him, that soul shall be cut off from my presence: I am the Lord.

- The Levitical priesthood was established in Aaron and his sons. Certain things were consecrated that could not be touched by the rest of Israel, and a priest with his uncleanness upon him could not go unto the holy things, lest that soul be cut off from the presence of the Most High.
- Aaron was consecrated and anointed to minister in the priest's office, and his sons were clothed and anointed as their father, an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations.

  Precepts:
  - **[Exodus 40:13-15](/bible/exodus/40#v13)**
    > <sup>[13](/bible/exodus/40#v13)</sup> And thou shalt put upon Aaron the holy garments, and anoint him, and sanctify him; that he may minister unto me in the priest’s office.
    >
    > <sup>[14](/bible/exodus/40#v14)</sup> And thou shalt bring his sons, and clothe them with coats:
    >
    > <sup>[15](/bible/exodus/40#v15)</sup> And thou shalt anoint them, as thou didst anoint their father, that they may minister unto me in the priest’s office: for their anointing shall surely be an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations.

    Aaron and his sons were anointed and sanctified to minister in the priest's office, an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations.

**[Leviticus 22:4-9](/bible/leviticus/22#v4)**

> <sup>[4](/bible/leviticus/22#v4)</sup> What man soever of the seed of Aaron is a leper, or hath a running issue; he shall not eat of the holy things, until he be clean. And whoso toucheth any thing that is unclean by the dead, or a man whose seed goeth from him;
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/leviticus/22#v5)</sup> Or whosoever toucheth any creeping thing, whereby he may be made unclean, or a man of whom he may take uncleanness, whatsoever uncleanness he hath;
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/leviticus/22#v6)</sup> The soul which hath touched any such shall be unclean until even, and shall not eat of the holy things, unless he wash his flesh with water.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/leviticus/22#v7)</sup> And when the sun is down, he shall be clean, and shall afterward eat of the holy things; because it is his food.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/leviticus/22#v8)</sup> That which dieth of itself, or is torn with beasts, he shall not eat to defile himself therewith: I am the Lord.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/leviticus/22#v9)</sup> They shall therefore keep mine ordinance, lest they bear sin for it, and die therefore, if they profane it: I the Lord do sanctify them.

- A man of the seed of Aaron that was a leper, had a running issue, or touched any unclean thing could not eat of the holy things until he was clean: he washed his flesh with water, and when the sun was down he was clean and could afterward eat.
- That which dieth of itself, or is torn with beasts, he shall not eat to defile himself therewith. That same law elsewhere says to give such a thing unto the stranger or sell it to an alien, for thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: these laws were given to Israel alone, and the other nations may eat those things because they are not the holy people. There is no equality in that.

  Precepts:
  - **[Deuteronomy 14:21](/bible/deuteronomy/14#v21)**
    > <sup>[21](/bible/deuteronomy/14#v21)</sup> Ye shall not eat of any thing that dieth of itself: thou shalt give it unto the stranger that is in thy gates, that he may eat it; or thou mayest sell it unto an alien: for thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God. Thou shalt not seethe a kid in his mother’s milk.

    The thing that dieth of itself may be given to the stranger or sold to an alien, for thou art an holy people; the law marks the difference between Israel and the nations.

**[Leviticus 22:10-16](/bible/leviticus/22#v10)**

> <sup>[10](/bible/leviticus/22#v10)</sup> There shall no stranger eat of the holy thing: a sojourner of the priest, or an hired servant, shall not eat of the holy thing.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/leviticus/22#v11)</sup> But if the priest buy any soul with his money, he shall eat of it, and he that is born in his house: they shall eat of his meat.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/leviticus/22#v12)</sup> If the priest’s daughter also be married unto a stranger, she may not eat of an offering of the holy things.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/leviticus/22#v13)</sup> But if the priest’s daughter be a widow, or divorced, and have no child, and is returned unto her father’s house, as in her youth, she shall eat of her father’s meat: but there shall no stranger eat thereof.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/leviticus/22#v14)</sup> And if a man eat of the holy thing unwittingly, then he shall put the fifth part thereof unto it, and shall give it unto the priest with the holy thing.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/leviticus/22#v15)</sup> And they shall not profane the holy things of the children of Israel, which they offer unto the Lord;
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/leviticus/22#v16)</sup> Or suffer them to bear the iniquity of trespass, when they eat their holy things: for I the Lord do sanctify them.

- No stranger may eat of the holy thing, neither a sojourner of the priest nor an hired servant. But the soul the priest buys with his money, and he that is born in his house, they eat of his meat, because they are joined to the priest's household.
- The priest's daughter married unto a stranger may not eat of the offering of the holy things; but if she is a widow or divorced and has no child, and is returned unto her father's house as in her youth, she eats of her father's meat, because she returns to her father's covering.
- A woman was commonly under her father's covering until she came under a husband's. The independent woman was not birthed from the Bible; she was birthed from Babylon.
- He that eats of the holy thing unwittingly adds the fifth part unto it and gives it to the priest with the holy thing; the priests must not suffer the children of Israel to bear the iniquity of trespass when they eat their holy things.

**[Leviticus 22:17-25](/bible/leviticus/22#v17)**

> <sup>[17](/bible/leviticus/22#v17)</sup> And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/leviticus/22#v18)</sup> Speak unto Aaron, and to his sons, and unto all the children of Israel, and say unto them, Whatsoever he be of the house of Israel, or of the strangers in Israel, that will offer his oblation for all his vows, and for all his freewill offerings, which they will offer unto the Lord for a burnt offering;
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/leviticus/22#v19)</sup> Ye shall offer at your own will a male without blemish, of the beeves, of the sheep, or of the goats.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/leviticus/22#v20)</sup> But whatsoever hath a blemish, that shall ye not offer: for it shall not be acceptable for you.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/leviticus/22#v21)</sup> And whosoever offereth a sacrifice of peace offerings unto the Lord to accomplish his vow, or a freewill offering in beeves or sheep, it shall be perfect to be accepted; there shall be no blemish therein.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/leviticus/22#v22)</sup> Blind, or broken, or maimed, or having a wen, or scurvy, or scabbed, ye shall not offer these unto the Lord, nor make an offering by fire of them upon the altar unto the Lord.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/leviticus/22#v23)</sup> Either a bullock or a lamb that hath any thing superfluous or lacking in his parts, that mayest thou offer for a freewill offering; but for a vow it shall not be accepted.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/leviticus/22#v24)</sup> Ye shall not offer unto the Lord that which is bruised, or crushed, or broken, or cut; neither shall ye make any offering thereof in your land.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/leviticus/22#v25)</sup> Neither from a stranger’s hand shall ye offer the bread of your God of any of these; because their corruption is in them, and blemishes be in them: they shall not be accepted for you.

- Whatever offering is brought for a vow or a freewill offering must be a male without blemish, of the beeves, of the sheep, or of the goats. Beeves goes to the ox and that family, the oxen and bulls.
- Blind, broken, maimed, or having a wen, or scurvy, or scabbed, shall not be offered unto the Lord. Scurvy is just having scratches; these offerings could have no scratches and no bruises, nothing bruised or crushed or broken or cut.
- Neither from a stranger's hand shall ye offer the bread of your God of any of these, because their corruption is in them and blemishes be in them; they shall not be accepted for you.

**[Leviticus 22:26-30](/bible/leviticus/22#v26)**

> <sup>[26](/bible/leviticus/22#v26)</sup> And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/leviticus/22#v27)</sup> When a bullock, or a sheep, or a goat, is brought forth, then it shall be seven days under the dam; and from the eighth day and thenceforth it shall be accepted for an offering made by fire unto the Lord.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/leviticus/22#v28)</sup> And whether it be cow or ewe, ye shall not kill it and her young both in one day.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/leviticus/22#v29)</sup> And when ye will offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving unto the Lord, offer it at your own will.
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/leviticus/22#v30)</sup> On the same day it shall be eaten up; ye shall leave none of it until the morrow: I am the Lord.

- When a bullock or a sheep or a goat is brought forth, it shall be seven days under the dam. The dam is that animal's mother; the young must stay under its mother seven days, and from the eighth day it is accepted for an offering.
- Whether it be cow or ewe, ye shall not kill it and her young both in one day. And the sacrifice of thanksgiving is eaten the same day; none of it is left until the morrow.

**[Leviticus 22:31-33](/bible/leviticus/22#v31)**

> <sup>[31](/bible/leviticus/22#v31)</sup> Therefore shall ye keep my commandments, and do them: I am the Lord.
>
> <sup>[32](/bible/leviticus/22#v32)</sup> Neither shall ye profane my holy name; but I will be hallowed among the children of Israel: I am the Lord which hallow you,
>
> <sup>[33](/bible/leviticus/22#v33)</sup> That brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God: I am the Lord.

- Therefore shall ye keep my commandments and do them: neither shall ye profane my holy name, but I will be hallowed among the children of Israel.
- I am the Lord which brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God. The Most High brought Israel out of the land of Egypt to be their God; that is the foundation the commandments stand on.
